title: Stationarity of a Prepared Machine State
statement: Let $A$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet and let $r$ be one of its states. Suppose that for every input symbol and every tuple of work-tape symbols, the transition from $r$ is the stationary control action that leaves the input head fixed, writes nothing, moves no work-tape head, emits no output, and returns to $r$. Then, for every input word $x$ and every configuration $c$ of the prepared machine on $x$ whose state is the copy of $r$ in the prepared machine's state space, one step leaves $c$ unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: Finite Turing machine $A$ over the Boolean alphabet
Every transition from $r$ is the stationary control action returning to $r$
Configuration $c$ in the prepared machine with state corresponding to $r$
replaced: If a control of the prepared machine is absorbing, its transition is the stationary control action, then the corresponding control of the loading-extended machine is absorbing as well, with the complete retained-input frame fixed.
